facts.raw_span: A 13-year-old boy presented with a 1-year history of pain and swelling around his right ankle
pain and swelling around his right ankle that had been gradually increasing in size
bony thickening over the lateral malleolus
the ankle and subtalar joints had a full range of motion
Complete blood count was within normal limits
erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 68 mm at the first hour
a submetaphyseal lytic lesion in the distal tibia with a well-defined sclerotic margin
Plain radiography of the right ankle revealed
a diagnosis of Brodie’s abscess was made
curettage was performed under spinal anesthesia via an anterior approach
Curetted material was sent for histopathological and microbiological assessment
